The CCTV evidence was rejected because it was not accompanied by a certificate as required by Section 106B(4) of the Evidence Act. [Ogembo v Yongo (Civil Appeal E200of2023) 2024KEHC15763(KLR) (9December2024) (Judgment), pp. 5–6]

claims.answer: The CCTV evidence was rejected because it was not accompanied by a certificate as required by Section 106B(4) of the Evidence Act.
claims.quote: “This provision makes it abundantly clear that for electronic evidence to be deemed admissible it must be accompanied by a certicate in terms of section 106B (4). Without the required certicate this CD is inadmissible as evidence.”

question: Who is qualified to sign a certificate of electronic evidence under section 106B(4) of the Evidence Act?

passage_detail.label: Evidence Act s.106B(4)
passage_detail.text_preview: ( 4 ) in any proceedings where it is desired to give a statement in evidence by virtue of this section, a certificate doing any of the following — ( a ) identifying the electronic record containing the statement and describing the manner in which it was produced ; ( b ) giving such particulars of an

answer:
Evidence Act s.106B(4)(d)

> ( d ) purporting to be signed by a person occupying a responsible position in relation to the operation of the relevant device or the management of the relevant activities ( whichever is appropriate ), shall be evidence of any matter stated in the certificate and for the purpose of this subsection it shall be sufficient for a matter to be stated to be the best of the knowledge of the person stating it.

> 12. Accordingly,  I  find  that  the  present  claim  is  founded  upon  an employer–employee  relationship  and  falls  within  the  exclusion contemplated under section 13(5) of the Small Claims Court Act. This Court consequently lacks jurisdiction to entertain the claim.
